newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge up 0.29 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge up 0.29 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares edged higher in thin and selective trade on Tuesday, despite profit-taking that followed the recent sharp gains, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed at a new all-time high of 88,335.02, up 255.16 points, or 0.29 percent from Monday's previous record of 88,079.86. But it was down from an early high of 88,799.
Trade volume plunged to 18.75 trillion lira from Monday's 26.24 trillion.
Brokers said last minute buying lifted the index to a new record although sellers were dominant for most of the day.
"Selling began after an early rise, but switching of shares prevented a major fluctuation in the index," said Attila Sozudogru from Soymen securities.
The index had gained 1.26 percent on Monday after a 5.38 percent surge last week when it pierced the stiff 85,000 barrier at its fourth attempt since late October.
Many brokers expect the market to drift sideways for a while before attempting the next major target at 90,000.

Of the 230 shares traded, 84 fell, 79 rose and 67 were steady. The 85-share industrial index .ISEI eased 0.15 percent to 92,599.27 while the 15-share financial index .ISEF gained 1.24 percent to 86,973.25.
Actives were led by T.Isbank's C series shares, up 1,000 lira at 18,250 and Turkish Airlines which also rose 1,000 lira to 28,000. Together, the two stocks made up 24.3 percent of the total volume.
